text: Why are interface toolkits single-threaded, given that `main` is not the event dispatch thread?
choices: Swing's components are immutable, so a second thread would have nothing to modify.
Repainting requires exclusive access to the display, which the operating system enforces.
A thread-safe widget hierarchy would need locking on every access, would be slow, and would deadlock — every toolkit tried and gave up.
The JVM permits only one thread to hold a native window handle at a time.
explanation: AWT was thread-safe, which is precisely why Swing is not. A repaint holding a lock while a handler waits for one is a classic deadlock. `invokeLater` and `invokeAndWait` post a `Runnable` onto the same queue the clicks go into. The dangerous part is that touching a component from the wrong thread usually appears to work, so it fails intermittently, under load, in ways that do not reproduce.
